# Case 211: Return Pointee Gained `const`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Verdict** | 🟠 **API_BREAK** |
| **Category** | API Break |
| **Classification** | Rule |
| **Platforms** | Linux |
| **Flags** | API break |
| **Detected `ChangeKind`s** | `func_return_pointee_qualifier_added` |
| **Source files** | `catalog/cases/case211_return_pointee_gained_const/` |
| **Rule family** | [`return-pointee-gained-const`](by-rule/return-pointee-gained-const.md) |
| **Subject** | [Function-signature and source-API changes](by-subject/function-signature-and-source-api-changes.md) |

**Category:** Source API | **Verdict:** 🟠 API_BREAK

## Verdict and consumer impact

`get_name()`'s return type changes from `char *` to `const char *`. Nothing
binary changes — the same pointer comes back in the same register — so every
prebuilt consumer keeps working after the library swap. Source compatibility
does break: a caller that stores the result in a plain `char *`, which v1's
declaration permits, no longer compiles against v2. In C++ that is a hard
error; in C it is a constraint violation (GCC 14+ rejects it by default,
GCC 13 and Clang warn and reject it under `-Werror`).

It is the return-value counterpart of
`case186_c_api_pointee_const_abi_neutral`.
There, a *parameter* pointee gaining `const` makes the callee promise more and
every direct call still compiles (a conditional risk). Here the qualifier
lands on what the *caller* receives, so the ordinary call pattern itself
breaks — an unconditional `API_BREAK`.

## Old/new diff

| v1.h | v2.h |
|------|------|
| `char *get_name(void);` | `const char *get_name(void);` |

## abicheck command

```bash
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v1.c -o libv1.so
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v2.c -o libv2.so
abicheck compare libv1.so libv2.so --header old=v1.h --header new=v2.h
```

## Expected abicheck finding

```text
Verdict: API_BREAK (exit 2)

func_return_pointee_qualifier_added: Return pointee qualifier added: get_name: char* → const char*
```

`func_return_changed` must not appear: the return type's binary
representation did not change. Verified identically with
`ABICHECK_AST_FRONTEND=castxml` and `ABICHECK_AST_FRONTEND=clang`.

## Minimum evidence

`min_evidence: L2` — C symbols carry no type, so the export table (L0) cannot
see it, and abicheck declines to read a pointee-qualifier change off DWARF
alone; the public header AST is the evidence tier the finding rests on.

## Why abicheck catches it

The header backends record each function's return type with its pointee
qualifiers. The return-type comparison separates a change confined to the
first-level pointee's `const`/`volatile` from a real change of the returned
type: a gained qualifier is `func_return_pointee_qualifier_added`
(`API_BREAK`), a dropped one `func_return_pointee_qualifier_removed`, and
neither is folded into `func_return_changed` (`BREAKING`).

## Runtime failure demonstration

**Severity: none at runtime; build failure on recompile.**

```bash
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v1.c -o libv1.so
gcc -g app.c -L. -lv1 -Wl,-rpath,'$ORIGIN' -o app
./app                                   # name = libname   exit 0
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v2.c -o libv1.so   # swap in v2, no recompile
./app                                   # name = libname   exit 0
```

The break shows up when the consumer is rebuilt against v2. The catalog's
`source_smoke` states it as a hard check under `-std=c11`:

```c
#include "v2.h"
_Static_assert(__builtin_types_compatible_p(__typeof__(get_name()), char *),
               "get_name() no longer returns char *: char *p = get_name(); breaks");
int main(void) { char *p = get_name(); return p != 0 ? 0 : 1; }
```

It compiles against `v1.h` and fails against `v2.h` with GCC and Clang.

## Safe redesign

Add a new accessor that returns `const char *` (`get_name_const()`) and keep
the old one's signature, or make the change at a major version with the
source break documented.

## Cross-tool comparison

`abidiff` reports a return-type subtype change (`char*` → `const char*`)
without separating binary from source impact; ABICC reports it in its
source-compatibility report only.
